headline_marked: [[Youth arrested over journalist Alif murder]] in Netrokona, police claim suspect admitted involvement
headline: Youth arrested over journalist Alif murder in Netrokona, police claim suspect admitted involvement
summary: Police arrested Opurba, 22, in Durgapur, Netrokona, on suspicion of involvement in the shooting death of journalist Lutfuzzaman Fakir alias Alif Fakir. Authorities claim he was present at the scene, carried the weapons, and admitted to the crime during initial
details: Police have arrested Opurba, 22, from Durgapur municipal town in Netrokona on suspicion of involvement in the shooting death of journalist Lutfuzzaman Fakir alias Alif Fakir. The arrest took place shortly after midnight on Saturday.

Khandaker Shaker Ahmed, officer-in-charge of Durgapur Police Station, confirmed the arrest. Police claim Opurba was present at the scene during the killing and was carrying the bag containing the weapons.
Authorities also stated that Opurba admitted to the crime during primary interrogation. He is reportedly the nephew of the prime suspect shooter, who is known as a contract for hire.

Information suggests the firearms used in the murder were kept in Opurba's custody. Police conducted a drive to arrest him after receiving a tip-off, as he reportedly hid during the day to evade capture.

The OC mentioned that Opurba was previously accused in a case filed last year for critically injuring journalist Alif Fakir. That incident involved hacking him with sharp weapons at Teribazar Ghat on November 10.

Journalist Lutfuzzaman Fakir Alif was shot dead by criminals around 8:15 PM on Thursday (October 15) while returning home. The incident occurred after he had tea at a stall in the Telanjia area of Durgapur upazila.
The victim's wife has filed a murder case with Durgapur Police Station. The case accuses seven to eight unidentified individuals in connection with the killing.

headline_marked: [[10 killed in Cox’s Bazar resort fire]]; family of four still missing, resort lacked clearances
headline: 10 killed in Cox’s Bazar resort fire; family of four still missing, resort lacked clearances
summary: A devastating fire at TUPTUP Resto and Resort in Cox’s Bazar claimed 10 lives, with a family of four still unaccounted for. Authorities revealed the resort operated without crucial fire safety and environmental clearances.
details: A devastating fire at TUPTUP Resto and Resort in Cox’s Bazar’s Ukhiya on Saturday morning claimed 10 lives, with a family of four still missing. The blaze, which took two hours to control, left bodies charred beyond recognition, necessitating DNA tests for identification.

Nahidur Rahman Tuhin, an official from Grand Power Limited, is among the missing, along with his wife Afsana and their two young daughters, Robaina (7) and Sunaina (3). Relatives have been unable to contact them since the fire erupted.

Nahidur had booked a room at the resort from October 16 to 18. His elder brother and company colleagues tried to reach him after learning of the fire but were unsuccessful, raising serious concerns for the family's safety.
Police and Fire Service officials reported that the fire broke out at approximately 6:30 AM. While several people were rescued alive, Nahidur's family does not appear on the list of survivors.

Cox’s Bazar Additional Police Superintendent Ahidur Rahman confirmed that Nahidur was known to be missing. Fire Service officials stated that six bodies were initially recovered, followed by four more from a toilet, including a child and two women.

The resort, located on Marine Drive in Inani’s Patuartek, was reportedly operating without essential fire safety and environmental clearances, according to Dhaka Tribune. This lack of compliance is now a key focus of the ongoing investigation.

DNA samples are currently being collected to identify the victims, as facial recognition is impossible due to the extent of the burns. Information on six missing individuals has been found, but four others remain unidentified.
